idea: um agente que lê logs de erro e abre tickets no Jira

areas.summary: Reads error logs and opens Jira tickets; success = every new error produces a Jira ticket within 15 minutes, with no duplicates for the same error.
The support team, 2-3 people, already use Jira daily and handle the tickets; non-engineer to moderate technical level.
v1 reads error logs and creates Jira tickets. Out of scope: fixing errors, closing or editing existing tickets, Slack/email alerts.
Plain-text error log files in a folder on the server, read every 10 minutes, up to about 50 MB per day.
One Jira Bug per distinct error in the support project: short title, summary, log excerpt, timestamp, occurrence count, suggested priority; read by the support team.

Connects to Jira Cloud REST API with an API token. If Jira is down, tickets wait in a local queue, retried 3 times with growing intervals, then an alert is written to the agent log. Test: if Jira returns 503, no ticket is lost and there are at most 3 retries.

Read-only access to the log folder; create-only access to Jira issues in the support project (no edit, close or delete). Secrets (Jira token, LLM API key) live in .env, never in code or logs. Test: if the code and agent logs are searched for the tokens, none are found, and an attempt to edit an existing ticket is refused.

Python 3.12 script run every 10 minutes by cron (or Windows Task Scheduler) on the same server as the logs; chosen for simple file handling and mature Jira/LLM libraries. Test: if the scheduler runs it, one run over a 50 MB log finishes in under 5 minutes.

One LLM step (Claude Haiku 5.5, claude-haiku-5-5) groups new error lines into distinct errors and writes title, summary and suggested priority; output is JSON {title, summary, priority: Highest|High|Medium|Low, fingerprint}. Test: if the model returns invalid JSON, the ticket is still created with a plain title from the log line and priority Medium.

Failure cases: (1) Jira down -> queue and retry 3 times; (2) wrong Jira credentials -> stop and alert, no retries; (3) empty or missing log file -> skip silently; (4) same error repeated -> update occurrence count in memory, no new ticket; (5) LLM fails or returns bad JSON -> fallback plain ticket; (6) unreadable/binary line -> skip and count. Test: if the same error appears 100 times in 10 minutes, exactly one ticket exists.

One Given/When/Then per requirement and per failure case, plus one happy path: Given a log file with a new error, when the agent runs, then one Jira Bug with all fields exists within 15 minutes. Test: if the happy-path test runs against a Jira test project, the ticket has title, summary, log excerpt, timestamp, count and priority.

Done when: all acceptance tests pass; every new error produces one ticket within 15 minutes with no duplicates; the support team ran it on last week's logs and the tickets looked right. Test: if it runs on last week's logs, the number of tickets equals the number of distinct errors and the team confirms them.

history.question: Como sabes que o agente está a funcionar bem: o que tem de acontecer a cada erro novo nos logs?
history.recommended: Cada erro novo gera um ticket no Jira em menos de 15 minutos, sem duplicados para o mesmo erro.

history.question: Quem vai ver e tratar estes tickets no dia a dia?
history.recommended: A tua equipa de suporte, 2 a 3 pessoas, que já usa o Jira todos os dias.

history.question: O que fica de fora da primeira versão?
history.recommended: Não corrige erros, não fecha nem edita tickets existentes, e não envia alertas por Slack ou email.

history.question: De onde vêm os logs de erro e de quanto em quanto tempo o agente os deve ler?
history.recommended: Ficheiros de texto numa pasta do servidor, lidos a cada 10 minutos, até cerca de 50 MB por dia.

history.question: O que deve ter cada ticket no Jira?
history.recommended: Um Bug no projeto de suporte, com título curto do erro, resumo, excerto do log, data/hora, número de ocorrências e prioridade sugerida.

history.question: Queres que eu assuma o resto? Cada suposição terá um teste que vais aprovar.
